mood: Cool, nonchalant, mid-tempo storytelling with a dry, ironic edge.
transcript: Three letters started a decade-long fight over the internet. In two thousand, ICM Registry asks ICANN, the internet's address office, for dot xxx. The pitch: give adult sites their own neighborhood. A red-light district with a zip code. ICANN says no. ICM tries again in two thousand four. This time, ICANN almost says yes. Then the inbox fills up. Family groups object. Countries object. The U.S. government sends a letter. ICANN votes no in two thousand seven. ICM, not taking the hint, demands an independent review. In twenty ten, the panel sides with ICM. In March twenty eleven, ICANN finally says yes. [short pause] Plot twist. Plenty of adult companies hated it too. A labeled neighborhood is easier to fence off. Then the brands panicked. Companies and universities paid to block their names, just in case. [deadpan] So somewhere, a very respectable university paid good money for a dot xxx that leads nowhere. Three letters. A decade of fighting. [short pause] And the most loyal customers just wanted to stay out.
